actions.action: Remove the basil from its pot and tease the crowded seedlings apart
Alternatively, soak the root ball in a bowl of water for a couple of minutes to loosen the seedlings
Pot each seedling individually in small pots with drainage holes, using coco coir/perlite mix or compost
Water the newly potted seedlings until water drains from the bottom
Place the plants somewhere bright and warm, such as a sunny south-facing window, getting 6+ hours of sun
Prune growing tips just above a leaf pair each time two new sets of leaves grow
Propagate pruned cuttings in a glass of water after stripping the lower leaves, kept bright but out of direct sun
Pot up rooted cuttings once the roots are a few cm long
Buy a clip-on grow light and run it for 12 hours a day
Keep the plant above 12°C, away from cold window sills at night and from radiators
Check soil moisture with a moisture meter
When the soil is drying, give the plant a proper soak without leaving it waterlogged
Feed regularly with a balanced liquid fertilizer, especially if the leaves are pale or yellowing

verdict.reason: The generic basil video blames overcrowding and only mentions drying out as a general care point, so the soaking fix is buried among repotting, pruning and light advice; nothing it suggests is likely to harm the plant.
